heat treatment of Escherichiae coli causes the release of part of lipopolysac-charide from the outer membrane, and this results in the disorganization of outer membrane structure and the disruption of permeability barrier function.

the effects of heat treatment on the permeability of the outer membrane in E. coli and with the mechanism of this heat-induced permeation of the outer membrane.

the effect of heat on the permeability barrier of the outer membrane and with the effect of Tris on the permeability properties of the outer membrane of Escherichiae coli.

heat treatment at 55 degrees caused a partial disruption of the outer membrane of E. coli, resulting in an increased hydrophobicity and a loss of the outer membrane barrier function.

the outer membrane of heat-treated cells became leaky to the hydrophobics, and the cells lost their resistance to the action of phospholipase.
the outer membrane of E. coli cells is destroyed by heating at 55 degrees or 60 degrees C, and that Tris-hydrogen chloride buffer at pH 7.0 or 8.0 enhances the destruction of the outer membrane.

heat treatment of E. coli at 55 degrees Celsius in the absence of Mg(2+) or HEPES resulted in the release of part of lipopolysacchride molecules from outer membranes and the disorganization of outer membranes and the permeability barrier functions of outer membranes.
